_doc: Single source for the atlas worker protocol: the cheap mechanical tier, the fixed report every atlas worker returns. Read by hooks/dispatch_tripwire.py (mechanicalTier only: STEPS: is required and capped at maxSteps for the mechanical agent; the six required dispatch blocks, REPORT: included, live in its REQUIRED_SPEC_BLOCKS and nowhere else), hooks/worker_report_gate.py (Claude Code SubagentStop check of the final message: container shape plus cheap objective checks on STEPS, EVIDENCE and FILES_CHANGED) and omp/worker-report.ts (injects the report outputSchema, strict, into atlas task items on omp). The tier is chosen by the lead through the agent name: runner = mechanical (exact steps, no decisions), implementer and explorer = standard (bounded work from a stated spec), verifier and the audit agents = judgment. Claude Code tiers are the agent frontmatter model and effort; omp tiers are role aliases resolved through modelRoles with the built-in @smol as the guaranteed fallback (omp ships smol, not tiny); every Claude haiku-pinned agent (runner, docs-auditor, schema-inventory, naming-glossary-audit) maps to the mechanical role, not only runner.

report.nativeWake: Optional, env-gated: when the lead exports ATLAS_LEAD_AGENT (its lead session name), after posting the board note also send the same report text via SendMessage (to: that name) as a best-effort native wake. The board note stays the transport of record; do not retry sends; skip entirely when the var is unset or the session is not listed.
report.taskMirror: Optional, env-gated: when the lead exports ATLAS_TASKS_MIRROR (truthy: 1/true/on), and a TaskCreate tool is available, mirror the board item you claim — TaskCreate with subject "[<phase>] <content>" at claim time, marked completed when you post your completion. The atlas board remains the source of truth; do not duplicate status updates beyond the one completion; skip entirely when the var is unset or off.

channels.model: Main channel per project: <cwd-basename>@<branch> (detached HEAD: @<short-sha>; non-git: basename). A lead that dispatches subagents gets the subchannel <main>/<lead-name> (opened at its first dispatch); its subagents are members with parent=lead. Notes carry a channel; to=all reaches the channel's members only, never another project/branch or another lead's subchannel. The lead is a member of its subchannel and of main and reads its members' todo board with `atlas_todo.py channel-board <channel>`.
channels.worker: A dispatched worker finds a CHANNEL: block in its brief with its exact post and inbox commands. Post with `atlas_todo.py note --channel <ch> --owner <you> --to <sibling|lead|all>`; read with `atlas_todo.py inbox --owner <you>` between steps where the PostToolUse inbox hook is not active (omp subagents: the hook resolves the agent id the bridge sends as agent_name, else run inbox yourself).

collab.rules: Path claims: before editing any file run `atlas_todo.py claim-paths --channel <ch> --owner <you> --paths <file,dir,...>` for the files you will touch (run `conflicts --owner <you> --paths ...` first). On conflict a kind:'conflict' note is posted to the owning sibling: message them and wait or pick other work — never edit a path another worker holds. Release with `release-paths` when done. Post `note --kind handoff --item <id> --to <consumer> "<result>"` when finishing a slice another worker consumes. Post `note --kind blocked --to <lead|peer> "<what you need>"` instead of idling. Never skip tests or verification because a peer said they passed. Only the lead declares work done.
